renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_volcano
  title: Exon shift against significance per gene
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: the relative log2 fold change of its most significant exon on the horizontal axis and the FDR of the gene-level F-test on the vertical axis, coloured by the direction of the call. It answers which genes show differential exon usage and which way the top exon moves.
    How to read: genes high on the plot have at least one exon behaving differently from the rest of the gene. A large shift of one exon with a modest FDR can still be real, so open the table tile for the Simes FDR and the number of exons called. An FDR of exactly zero is drawn at the top of the axis.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an FDR of 0.05, the cut-off of this table's significance call: the recipe parameter fdr, which the rnasplice template sets from its SPLICING_FDR variable (default 0.05). It is a template default, not a value read from edgeR, and no fold-change line is drawn because the call uses none.
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 0.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Top exon log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 FDR of the gene test
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: fdr
    label: gene_id
    category: direction

- component: card
  title: Genes tested
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes tested for differential exon usage, and the ring splits them by the direction of their most significant exon. It answers how many genes pass the call and which way they move.
    How to read: a large share of not significant genes is normal, since most genes use their exons alike. A ring with only one direction points to a shared bias such as a library effect.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: genes, by direction of the top exon

- component: card
  title: Significant exons
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of exons called significant across genes, and the box shows how many each gene contributes. It answers whether usage changes sit on a single exon or spread over the gene.
    How to read: a gene with many exons called suggests a gene-wide shift, which can reflect an isoform switch or a coverage artefact. A gene with one or two exons called is the typical exon-skipping pattern.
  column: exons_significant
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: exons called per gene, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Size of the exon shift
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median absolute relative log2 fold change of the top exon per gene, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how strong the exon-level differences are.
    How to read: a box close to zero means most genes show only small shifts. Filter to significant genes with the volcano to see the size of the real effects.
  column: abs_log2fc
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the absolute log2 fold change

- component: interactive
  title: Direction of the top exon
  description: Restricts every tile to genes whose top exon goes up, goes down or does not change significantly.
    It answers whether a pattern belongs to one direction.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: direction

- component: table
  title: Genes with differential exon usage
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast, with its exon counts, top exon, fold change, F-test FDR and Simes FDR. It answers which genes to inspect exon by exon.
    How to read: sort by FDR, or by the Simes FDR when one exon carries the change, and select a row to filter the dashboard to the gene.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id
